baseline:
B
A standard Transformer block consists of two primary sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise feedforward neural network (which is a type of MLP).

B
An MLP is characterized by having one or more hidden layers between its input and output layers. The use of non-linear activation functions in these layers is crucial, as it enables the network to learn complex, non-linear patterns.

B
The MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron), also known as the Feed-Forward Network in a transformer block, takes the context-aware embeddings produced by the attention mechanism and applies a non-linear transformation. This allows the model to process the information gathered by attention in a more complex way, enriching the representation of each token before it is passed to the next layer.

C
The MLP's weights are adjusted during training to encode factual knowledge, effectively learning to map specific input patterns (keys) to corresponding output patterns (values), thus acting as a form of associative memory.

C
The core of a neural network's learning process is finding the optimal values for its weights (W) and biases (b). These parameters are adjusted during training to minimize error, and in doing so, they encode the patterns and relationships from the training data. They are, in essence, the memory of the model.
